bibl.title: CAR-T cell therapy: current limitations and potential strategies

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: chimeric antigen receptor T cells - engineered synthetic receptors that redirect T cells onto a chosen surface antigen - and what stops them working
span.quote: CARs are engineered synthetic receptors that function to redirect lymphocytes, most commonly T cells, to recognize and eliminate cells expressing a specific target antigen.

span.label: which limitations of CAR-T therapy are structural and which are engineering problems with proposed solutions
span.quote: However, there are major limitations to CAR-T cell therapy that still must be addressed including life-threatening CAR-T cell-associated toxicities, limited efficacy against solid tumors, inhibition and resistance in B cell malignancies, antigen escape, limited persistence, poor trafficking and tumor infiltration, and the immunosuppressive microenvironment.

span.label: a review pairing each named limitation with the engineering strategies proposed against it, and stating plainly which parts of the construct are not understood
span.quote: Barriers to effective CAR-T cell therapy include severe life-threatening toxicities, modest anti-tumor activity, antigen escape, restricted trafficking, and limited tumor infiltration.

span.label: critique
span.quote: However, there are major limitations to CAR-T cell therapy that still must be addressed including life-threatening CAR-T cell-associated toxicities, limited efficacy against solid tumors, inhibition and resistance in B cell malignancies, antigen escape, limited persistence, poor trafficking and tumor infiltration, and the immunosuppressive microenvironment.

span.label: MHC-independent T cell activation against a surface antigen, powerful in B cell malignancies and limited nearly everywhere else
span.quote: CAR binding to target antigens expressed on the cell surface is independent from the MHC receptor resulting in vigorous T cell activation and powerful anti-tumor responses

span.label: narrative review of CAR construct engineering - antigen-binding domain, hinge, transmembrane domain, signalling domains - against the clinical limitations
span.term: narrative review of CAR construct engineering - antigen-binding domain, hinge, transmembrane domain, signalling domains - against the clinical limitations
span.quote: The hinge or spacer region is defined as the extracellular structural region that extends the binding units from the transmembrane domain.

span.label: the CAR binds a surface antigen INDEPENDENTLY OF MHC, which is what makes the activation vigorous and also what removes the presentation step that normally restricts a T cell response
span.quote: CAR binding to target antigens expressed on the cell surface is independent from the MHC receptor resulting in vigorous T cell activation and powerful anti-tumor responses

span.label: the hinge sets the distance between the binding domain and the membrane, and therefore which epitopes are reachable: long spacers for membrane-proximal epitopes, short ones for membrane-distal
span.quote: In principle, the “optimal” spacer length is dependent on the position of the target epitope and the level of steric hindrance on the target cell in which long spacers provide added flexibility and allow more effective access to membrane-proximal epitopes or complex glycosylated antigens, while short hinges are more successful at binding membrane-distal epitopes

span.label: IgG-derived spacers interact with Fc-gamma receptors and cause CAR-T cell depletion, so a choice made for geometry has an immunological cost the geometry does not predict
span.quote: IgG-derived spacers, however, can cause CAR-T cell depletion and thus, decreased persistence in vivo as they can interact with Fcγ

span.label: the two approved co-stimulatory domains produce different T cell fates and different metabolisms - CD28 gives effector memory and aerobic glycolysis, 4-1BB gives central memory and oxidative metabolism
span.quote: The co-stimulatory domains differ in their functional and metabolic profiles in which CARs with CD28 domains differentiate into effector memory T cells and primarily use aerobic glycolysis while CARs possessing the 4-1BB domain differentiate into central memory T cells and display increased mitochondrial biogenesis and oxidative metabolism 32 .

span.label: antigen escape: the tumour survives by losing the one thing the CAR was built to see
span.quote: Although initially single antigen targeting CAR-T cells can deliver high response rates, the malignant cells of a significant portion of patients treated with these CAR-T cells display either partial or complete loss of target antigen expression.

span.label: CRS is believed to be mediated primarily by IL-6, which is why blocking the IL-6 receptor is the treatment
span.quote: Pathophysiologically, CRS is believed to be primarily mediated by IL-6 and therefore, management relies on the use of IL-6 receptor blockade with tocilizumab and corticosteroids 3 – 5 .

span.label: lowering the binding domain's affinity raises the antigen density needed to trigger the cell, so normal tissue expressing a little antigen is spared
span.quote: Decreasing the affinity of the antigen-binding domain would be expected to result in an increased requirement for higher antigen density on tumor cells in order for high levels of activation to be achieved.

span.label: engineering the T cells to express heparanase lets them digest the proteoglycan barrier and enter the tumour
span.quote: CAR-T cells that have been engineered to express heparanase, an enzyme that degrades HSPG, show enhanced tumor infiltration and antitumor activity 68 .

span.label: matching chemokine receptors on the CAR-T cell to the chemokines the tumour actually emits improves trafficking
span.quote: One recently developed strategy that appears to significantly improve CAR-T cell trafficking involves expressing chemokine receptors on CAR-T cells that match and respond to tumor-derived chemokines 64 .

span.label: neutralising GM-CSF lowers neurotoxicity and CRS while INCREASING CAR-T cell activity - the toxicity and the effect come apart
span.quote: Recent preclinical studies have demonstrated that neurotoxicity and CRS are decreased and CAR-T cell activity is increased after inhibition of macrophage activating and monocyte activating cytokine GM-CSF with lenzilumab 87 , 98 , 99 .

span.label: local delivery removes the trafficking problem and the off-tumour problem at once, because the cells never circulate
span.quote: One strategy to ameliorate these limitations is through the utilization of delivery routes other than systemic delivery as local administration (1) eliminates the need for CAR-T cells to traffic to disease sites and (2) limits on-target off-tumor toxicities as the CAR-T cells’ on-target activity is directed on tumor cells minimizing interaction with normal tissues 60 .

span.label: IN PRINCIPLE VS IN PRACTICE, AND THE PAPER PUTS `OPTIMAL` IN SCARE QUOTES ITSELF: the optimal spacer length follows from epitope position and steric hindrance, and IN PRACTICE IS OFTEN DETERMINED EMPIRICALLY and tailored per antigen-binding pair
span.quote: In practice, however, the proper spacer length is often determined empirically and must be tailored for each specific antigen-binding domain pair.

span.label: the transmembrane domain is PROBABLY THE LEAST CHARACTERIZED REGION of the whole construct - a component named in every design and studied in almost none
span.quote: Among all of the components of CAR’s, the transmembrane domain is probably the least characterized region.

span.label: AND THE REASON IS GIVEN, WHICH IS RARE: the effect of one transmembrane domain against another is not well studied BECAUSE THE DOMAIN IS FREQUENTLY CHANGED to suit the spacer or the signalling domains. A part cannot be measured while it is being used as the adjustment
span.quote: The effect of one transmembrane compared to another on CAR function is not well studied as the transmembrane domain is frequently changed based on the requirements of the extracellular spacer region or the intracellular signaling domains.

span.label: affinity does not explain its own effect: scFvs WITH SIMILAR AFFINITIES can differentially impact CAR-T cell function, so the measured quantity underdetermines the behaviour it is chosen for
span.quote: While affinity is certainly one of the most important factors to further complicate matters, it has been shown that even scFvs with similar affinities can differentially impact CAR-T cell function.

span.label: the limitation list is clinical and long - toxicities, poor efficacy in solid tumours, antigen escape, limited persistence, poor trafficking and infiltration, the immunosuppressive microenvironment
span.quote: However, there are major limitations to CAR-T cell therapy that still must be addressed including life-threatening CAR-T cell-associated toxicities, limited efficacy against solid tumors, inhibition and resistance in B cell malignancies, antigen escape, limited persistence, poor trafficking and tumor infiltration, and the immunosuppressive microenvironment.

span.label: a limitation that is not biological at all: THE WORKFORCE must adapt, and the review counts training programmes among the barriers to the therapy
span.quote: In addition, the workforce must adapt to meet the needs of this growing and evolving field by developing educational programs to train a workforce

span.label: the mechanism of CAR-T neurotoxicity is stated as not understood, in a paper devoted to its limitations
span.quote: In the case of neurotoxicity, the underlying pathophysiology and mechanisms are not completely understood 88 .

span.label: the incidence of HLH/MAS cannot be given because it overlaps with high-grade CRS - the categories are not separable in the data
span.quote: While the incidence of HLH/MAS secondary to CAR-T cell therapy is unclear due to overlap with high-grade CRS, it has been reported in ≈1% of patients receiving CAR-T cell therapy 88 .

span.label: third-generation CARs with two co-stimulatory domains gave mixed results and failed to beat second-generation in two models
span.quote: Preclinical studies of third generation CARs have produced mixed results.

span.label: no approved therapy exists to PREVENT any of these toxicities - only to treat them once they occur
span.quote: To date, there remain no approved therapies for the prevention of the above toxicities, making it essential to optimize CAR engineering and employ other strategies to decrease CAR-induced toxicities 88 .

span.label: localised injection works better but is limited in principle to single or oligometastatic lesions
span.quote: Although localized injection appears to have superior efficacy, theoretically this approach is limited to single tumor lesions/oligometastatic disease 25 .

span.label: even combining CAR-T cells with checkpoint blockade may be insufficient to produce infiltration and effector function
span.quote: Although combination checkpoint blockade-CAR-T cell therapy is likely a new immunotherapy option, it is important to also recognize that even this combination may still be insufficient to induce infiltration of T cells and effector function.

span.label: the anti-CD19 result is held up as the case where the approach demonstrably works, against which every other target is measured
span.note: eliminates: a field-wide failure being read as a failure of the concept rather than of its application to harder targets · outcome: held
span.quote: The unprecedented success of anti-CD19 CAR-T cell therapy against B cell malignancies resulted in its approval by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in 2017

span.label: whether spacer length can be derived from epitope position and steric hindrance rather than found by trial
span.note: eliminates: nothing - the review states it is often determined empirically and must be tailored for each antigen-binding domain pair · outcome: failed
span.quote: In principle, the “optimal” spacer length is dependent on the position of the target epitope and the level of steric hindrance on the target cell in which long spacers provide added flexibility and allow more effective access to membrane-proximal epitopes or complex glycosylated antigens, while short hinges are more successful at binding membrane-distal epitopes

span.label: whether one transmembrane domain can be compared against another for its effect on CAR function
span.note: eliminates: nothing - the domain is frequently changed to suit the spacer and the signalling domains, so it is never the variable held constant · outcome: failed
span.quote: The effect of one transmembrane compared to another on CAR function is not well studied as the transmembrane domain is frequently changed based on the requirements of the extracellular spacer region or the intracellular signaling domains.

span.label: whether binding affinity accounts for CAR-T cell function
span.note: eliminates: nothing - scFvs with similar affinities differentially impact function, and the review lists epitope location, antigen density and tonic signalling as further factors that must be considered · outcome: failed
span.quote: While affinity is certainly one of the most important factors to further complicate matters, it has been shown that even scFvs with similar affinities can differentially impact CAR-T cell function.

span.label: CARs
span.quote: CARs are engineered synthetic receptors that function to redirect lymphocytes, most commonly T cells, to recognize and eliminate cells expressing a specific target antigen.

span.label: hinge
span.quote: The hinge or spacer region is defined as the extracellular structural region that extends the binding units from the transmembrane domain.

span.label: transmembrane domain
span.quote: The hinge or spacer region is defined as the extracellular structural region that extends the binding units from the transmembrane domain.

span.label: antigen escape
span.quote: However, there are major limitations to CAR-T cell therapy that still must be addressed including life-threatening CAR-T cell-associated toxicities, limited efficacy against solid tumors, inhibition and resistance in B cell malignancies, antigen escape, limited persistence, poor trafficking and tumor infiltration, and the immunosuppressive microenvironment.

span.label: affinity
span.quote: While affinity is certainly one of the most important factors to further complicate matters, it has been shown that even scFvs with similar affinities can differentially impact CAR-T cell function.

span.label: co-stimulatory domain
span.quote: second generation CARs with one co-stimulatory domain in series with the CD3 ζ intracellular signaling domain were generated 30 , 31 .

span.label: cytokine-release syndrome
span.quote: Mechanistically, CRS is a result of administered CAR-T cells becoming extensively activated resulting in the release of massive amounts of cytokines.

span.label: ICANS
span.quote: immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS), which is characterized by elevated cerebrospinal fluid cytokine levels and blood–brain barrier disruption 86 .

span.label: on-target off-tumor
span.quote: One of the challenges in targeting solid tumor antigens is that solid tumor antigens are often also expressed on normal tissues at varying levels.

span.label: tandem CARs
span.quote: These employ the use of either dual CAR constructs or tandem CARs, which is a single CAR construct that contains two scFvs in order to concomitantly target multiple target tumor antigens.

span.label: armored CARs
span.quote: Many studies have investigated numerous cytokines to create these “armored CARs”.

span.label: therapeutic window
span.quote: In other words, the CAR-T cell must remain within its therapeutic window to be clinically effective as overshooting the therapeutic window will lead to toxicity.

span.label: tumor stroma
span.quote: Stroma is mostly composed of extracellular matrix in which heparin sulfate proteoglycan (HSPG) is the primary component that CAR-T cells must degrade in order to pass into the tumor 67 .

span.label: `optimal` spacer length - AS USED HERE, TWICE OVER. In principle a derived quantity (epitope position, steric hindrance); in practice an empirical one, tailored per pair. THE PAPER'S OWN SCARE QUOTES MARK THE GAP - a property defined by a theory and decided by trying it
span.quote: In principle, the “optimal” spacer length is dependent on the position of the target epitope and the level of steric hindrance on the target cell in which long spacers provide added flexibility and allow more effective access to membrane-proximal epitopes or complex glycosylated antigens, while short hinges are more successful at binding membrane-distal epitopes

span.label: hinge / spacer region - defined structurally: the extracellular region extending the binding units from the transmembrane domain. A definition by POSITION, which is why its correct value is a length and why the length cannot be derived
span.quote: The hinge or spacer region is defined as the extracellular structural region that extends the binding units from the transmembrane domain.

span.label: transmembrane domain - the least characterised part of the construct, and the review explains the mechanism of that ignorance: it is the piece that gets changed whenever another piece needs to fit
span.quote: The effect of one transmembrane compared to another on CAR function is not well studied as the transmembrane domain is frequently changed based on the requirements of the extracellular spacer region or the intracellular signaling domains.

span.label: critiques → CAR-T therapy as a general cancer treatment, on the ground that its clinical success is confined to certain B cell malignancies while solid tumours resist it
span.quote: Barriers to effective CAR-T cell therapy include severe life-threatening toxicities, modest anti-tumor activity, antigen escape, restricted trafficking, and limited tumor infiltration.

span.label: critiques → affinity as the design variable for the antigen-binding domain, since scFvs with similar affinities behave differently
span.quote: While affinity is certainly one of the most important factors to further complicate matters, it has been shown that even scFvs with similar affinities can differentially impact CAR-T cell function.

span.label: supports → anti-CD19 CAR-T therapy, whose success is the reason the rest of the field exists - FDA approval in 2017
span.quote: The unprecedented success of anti-CD19 CAR-T cell therapy against B cell malignancies resulted in its approval by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in 2017

span.label: IN PRINCIPLE THE OPTIMAL SPACER LENGTH FOLLOWS FROM EPITOPE POSITION AND STERIC HINDRANCE; IN PRACTICE IT IS OFTEN DETERMINED EMPIRICALLY and tailored for each antigen-binding domain pair. The scare quotes on `optimal` are the paper's own
span.term: IN PRINCIPLE THE OPTIMAL SPACER LENGTH FOLLOWS FROM EPITOPE POSITION AND STERIC HINDRANCE; IN PRACTICE IT IS OFTEN DETERMINED EMPIRICALLY and tailored for each antigen-binding domain pair. The scare quotes on `optimal` are the paper's own
span.quote: In practice, however, the proper spacer length is often determined empirically and must be tailored for each specific antigen-binding domain pair.

span.label: the transmembrane domain is PROBABLY THE LEAST CHARACTERIZED REGION of the CAR, and the reason given is that it is frequently changed to suit the other parts - a component that is never the held-constant variable
span.term: the transmembrane domain is PROBABLY THE LEAST CHARACTERIZED REGION of the CAR, and the reason given is that it is frequently changed to suit the other parts - a component that is never the held-constant variable
span.quote: The effect of one transmembrane compared to another on CAR function is not well studied as the transmembrane domain is frequently changed based on the requirements of the extracellular spacer region or the intracellular signaling domains.

span.label: scFvs with SIMILAR AFFINITIES can differentially impact CAR-T cell function, so epitope location, target antigen density and tonic signalling must also be considered
span.term: scFvs with SIMILAR AFFINITIES can differentially impact CAR-T cell function, so epitope location, target antigen density and tonic signalling must also be considered
span.quote: While affinity is certainly one of the most important factors to further complicate matters, it has been shown that even scFvs with similar affinities can differentially impact CAR-T cell function.

span.label: IgG-derived spacers cause CAR-T cell depletion and decreased persistence in vivo because they interact with Fc-gamma receptors
span.term: IgG-derived spacers cause CAR-T cell depletion and decreased persistence in vivo because they interact with Fc-gamma receptors
span.quote: IgG-derived spacers, however, can cause CAR-T cell depletion and thus, decreased persistence in vivo as they can interact with Fcγ

span.label: the barrier list is clinical and structural at once - toxicities, modest anti-tumour activity, antigen escape, restricted trafficking, limited tumour infiltration
span.term: the barrier list is clinical and structural at once - toxicities, modest anti-tumour activity, antigen escape, restricted trafficking, limited tumour infiltration
span.quote: Barriers to effective CAR-T cell therapy include severe life-threatening toxicities, modest anti-tumor activity, antigen escape, restricted trafficking, and limited tumor infiltration.

span.label: A LIMITATION THAT IS NOT BIOLOGICAL: the workforce must adapt, and educational programmes to train it are counted among the things the field must build
span.term: A LIMITATION THAT IS NOT BIOLOGICAL: the workforce must adapt, and educational programmes to train it are counted among the things the field must build
span.quote: In addition, the workforce must adapt to meet the needs of this growing and evolving field by developing educational programs to train a workforce

span.label: most relapsed ALL patients respond to CD19 CAR-T therapy, and a large share of those who relapse afterwards have lost the CD19 antigen
span.quote: For example, although 70–90% of relapsed and/or refractory ALL patients show durable responses to CD19 targeted CAR-T cell therapy, recent follow-up data suggest development of a common disease resistance mechanism, including downregulation/loss of CD19 antigen in 30–70% of patients who have recurrent disease after treatment 42 , 43 .

span.label: nearly all ALL/LBL patients show some toxicity and roughly a quarter to a half show severe cytokine production with massive T cell expansion
span.quote: Specifically, in the case of acute lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma (ALL/LBL) patients treated with CAR-T cell therapy, nearly all patients have at least some less severe toxicity manifestations while 23–46% of patients displayed severe supraphysiologic cytokine production and massive in-vivo T cell expansion 85 .

span.label: any-grade CRS occurs in the large majority of leukaemia and lymphoma patients, with severe CRS far rarer and differing by product
span.quote: In total, 77–93% of patients with leukemia receiving CAR-T cell therapy and 37–93% of patients with lymphoma receiving CAR-T cell therapy had any grade of CRS while 46% of patients treated with tisagenlecleucel for relapsed/refractory B-ALL and 13–18% of patients treated with axicabtagene ciloleucel and tisagenlecleucel, respectively for diffuse large B-cell lymphoma had ≥Grade 3 CRS 3 , 4 .

span.label: neurotoxicity is common rather than exceptional, reaching two thirds of leukaemia patients
span.quote: Neurotoxicity following CAR-T cell therapy is relatively common and can occur in up to 67% and 62% of patients receiving treatment for leukemia and lymphoma, respectively 86 .

span.label: modifying the hinge and transmembrane region gave complete remission in over half a small lymphoma cohort with no CRS or ICANS above grade 1
span.quote: Optimizing the hinge and transmembrane regions could be a useful approach to decrease toxicity as in phase 1 clinical trial, these modified hinge and transmembrane region CARs resulted in complete remission in 54.5% of B cell lymphoma patients (6/11 patients), and importantly, there were no CRS or ICANS events grade >1 93 .

span.label: combining mesothelin-targeted CAR-T cells with anti-PD-1 produced a high response rate in mesothelioma including two complete metabolic responses
span.quote: One intriguing study in which 11 mesothelioma patients who received preconditioning with cyclophosphamide followed by a single dose of mesothelin targeted CAR-T cells and at least three doses of anti-PD-1agent resulted in a 72% response rate and complete metabolic responses in two patients 75 .

span.label: dual targeting beat single targeting in both glioblastoma and breast cancer preclinical models
span.quote: In both cases, dual targeting resulted in superior anti-tumor responses compared to single targeted therapy 28 , 52 .

span.label: engineered synthetic receptors that redirect lymphocytes, most commonly T cells, to recognize and eliminate cells expressing a specific target antigen
span.quote: CARs are engineered synthetic receptors that function to redirect lymphocytes, most commonly T cells, to recognize and eliminate cells expressing a specific target antigen.

span.label: the extracellular structural region that extends the binding units from the transmembrane domain
span.quote: The hinge or spacer region is defined as the extracellular structural region that extends the binding units from the transmembrane domain.

span.label: the three named toxicity syndromes, given as a numbered list with their defining features
span.quote: These toxic levels of systemic cytokine release and severe immune cell cross-activation in some patients result in the following toxicities: 1 cytokine-release syndrome (CRS), which is associated with supraphysiologic cytokine production and massive in vivo T cell expansion 2 hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis and/or macrophage activation syndrome (MAS) defined as a severe hyperinflammatory syndrome characterized by CRS and combinations of elevated serum ferritin and hemophagocytosis, renal failure, liver enzymes, splenomegaly, pulmonary edema, and/or absence of NK cell activity, and 3 immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS), which is characterized by elevated cerebrospinal fluid cytokine levels and blood–brain barrier disruption 86 .

span.label: the therapeutic window stated for CAR-T cells - a lower threshold for efficacy and an upper one for toxicity
span.quote: In order to achieve efficacious therapeutic responses, a CAR-T cell antigen-binding domain must bind its target epitope and reach a minimum threshold level to induce CAR-T cell activation and cytokine secretion.

span.label: the year anti-CD19 CAR-T therapy was approved by the FDA - the success the rest of the field is measured against
span.quote: The unprecedented success of anti-CD19 CAR-T cell therapy against B cell malignancies resulted in its approval by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in 2017

span.label: the share of recurrent ALL patients whose disease has downregulated or lost CD19
span.quote: For example, although 70–90% of relapsed and/or refractory ALL patients show durable responses to CD19 targeted CAR-T cell therapy, recent follow-up data suggest development of a common disease resistance mechanism, including downregulation/loss of CD19 antigen in 30–70% of patients who have recurrent disease after treatment 42 , 43 .

span.label: the incidence of HLH/MAS after CAR-T cell therapy
span.quote: While the incidence of HLH/MAS secondary to CAR-T cell therapy is unclear due to overlap with high-grade CRS, it has been reported in ≈1% of patients receiving CAR-T cell therapy 88 .

span.label: the upper bound of neurotoxicity incidence in leukaemia and lymphoma
span.quote: Neurotoxicity following CAR-T cell therapy is relatively common and can occur in up to 67% and 62% of patients receiving treatment for leukemia and lymphoma, respectively 86 .

span.label: affinity
span.quote: While affinity is certainly one of the most important factors to further complicate matters, it has been shown that even scFvs with similar affinities can differentially impact CAR-T cell function.

span.label: spacer length
span.quote: In practice, however, the proper spacer length is often determined empirically and must be tailored for each specific antigen-binding domain pair.

span.label: epitope location
span.quote: Therefore, in order to optimize binding of the CAR to its target antigen, additional factors such as epitope location, target antigen density, and avoidance of scFvs associated with ligand-independent tonic signaling must be considered.

span.label: the factors stated to govern CAR-T activation kinetics: antigen expression level, tumour burden, binding affinity and the co-stimulatory elements
span.quote: From an engineering perspective, the degree of CAR-T cell activation and activation kinetics are influenced by several factors including but not limited to the level of tumor antigen expressed on malignant cells, tumor burden, antigen binding domain’s affinity to its target epitope, and the CAR’s costimulatory elements 33 , 92 .

span.label: the factors stated to determine toxicity incidence and severity: CAR design, target, and tumour type
span.quote: Critical factors that likely determine the incidence and severity of CRS, HLH/MAS, and/or ICANS are the design of the CAR, the specific target, and the tumor type 81 .

p.note: The full text of this article is not redistributable, so it is not included here. Every tag above carries the exact sentence it was made from, quoted under fair quotation. The article itself is at https://doi.org/10.1038/s41408-021-00459-7.
